From previous experience, a museum guide knows the mean number of visitors per hour is $5.5$. However, he thinks that attendance has reduced due to a decrease in teen interest in history. Let $X$ represent the number of visitors during a particular hour. Under the null hypothesis that the number of visitors is the same as before, what is the critical region of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $10%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **cumulative distribution function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $⋯$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X \le x)$ | $0.0041$ | $0.0266$ | $0.0884$ | $0.2017$ | $0.3575$ | $0.5289$ | $⋯$ |

Josh plays chess online, winning $67%$ of the games. He has just found a new platform for playing chess and suspects the players enrolled are stronger. Let $X$ represent the number of games Josh will win out of $5$ games on the new platform. Under the null hypothesis that Josh's proportion of won games is the same, what is the critical region of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $10%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **cumulative distribution function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X \le x)$ | $0.0039$ | $0.0436$ | $0.2050$ | $0.5325$ | $0.8650$ | $1.0000$ |
